label: p/q/g/3 input mid-way through the original phase, boosted by early e/f/r/n/o/c/h/k/d tokens
explanation: Fires only in the original (input) phase, never at t<2, at the delimiter, or during copy. It peaks at t=4-6. The current input token is the main driver: p (lift 12x, 46% of mass), then q, g, and digit 3. Together these four tokens hold about 93% of the mass, and the strongest activations are almost all on p. Mostly first occurrences of the token. Whether it fires on those tokens depends on what came earlier: rates are much higher when the sequence begins with, or has already seen, tokens from {e,f,r,n,o,c,h,k,d}. First token e is strongest, about 4x. This looks like a graded hidden-state dependence, and a boolean predicate only approximates it. On dev, plain (original phase, t>=3, token p/q/g/3) gets mass recall 0.91 but precision 0.24. Adding the history condition raises precision to 0.34 (F1 0.46, mass recall 0.81). Weak, rare firing also occurs on s, t, 2, and i.
